To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Botrytis produces ethylene by a novel biosynthetic pathway.
Botrytis produces ethylene by photo-oxidation of a precursor, KMBA, and that this precursor is produced in darkness.

(i) Botrytis produces ethylene during the first 48 hours of culture, (ii) Botrytus uses methionine as a precursor of ethylene, (iii) Botrytiscinerea uses the same biosynthetic pathway as plants, and (iv) Botrytisinerea produces alpha-keto gamma- methylthiobutyrate acid (KMBA), which is photo-oxidised to ethylene
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biosynthesis of ethylene by B. cinera.
the role of ethylene in plant-pathogen interactions.
ethylene biosynthesis in B. cinerea, a phytopathogenic fungus that produces ethylene.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ethylene biosynthesis pathway of B. cinerea involves the production of KMBA by methionine, and the photo-oxidation of KMBA to ethylene in light.
ethylene production by B. cinerae is not a consequence of the infection process.
the fungus B. cinerea produces ethylene in the dark by the action of a peroxidase, and in light by the photo-oxidation of KMBA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ethylene biosynthetic pathway in B. cinerea involves methionine and the intermediate alpha-keto gamma- methylthiobutyraldehyde (KMTBA), which is oxidized to KMBA by an NAD-dependent dehydrogenase (EC 1.1.1.298).
the fungus B. cinerea produces KMBA and ethylene in vitro, and that ethylene is formed in darkness by the action of peroxidase.
ethylene is not a major player in B. cinerea infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
B. cinerea produces and releases KMBA, the precursor of ethylene, during growth in culture.
B. cinerea is capable of producing ethylene and that ethylene production is affected by the presence of light.
ethylene is produced in darkness by B. cinere, and that this production is enhanced in the presence of peroxidases.
